finding.summary: weizigo_showscores panicked on any 4x4 board under a safe build: formatShowScores formatted a value with bufPrint directly INTO out_buf and then copied the returned slice onto its own backing memory with @memcpy. bufPrint returns a slice of the buffer it wrote into, so source and destination were the same bytes; Zig's overlap check trapped with 'panic: @memcpy arguments alias'. The crash was first seen by T327, recorded only in its close note, and never filed; T366 hit it again (worked around by reading L/H through the session API). T374 filed and fixed it.
finding.root_cause:
const s1 = std.fmt.bufPrint(out_buf[off..][0..3], "{d:>3}", .{v}) catch {...}; @memcpy(out_buf[off .. off + s1.len], s1);

The formatted bytes were already in place: bufPrint writes into out_buf[off..][0..3] and returns a slice of that same memory. The @memcpy was a no-op with identical source and destination, and the copy was never needed.
finding.fix: Deleted the @memcpy entirely (minimal; the formatted bytes are already where the renderer needs them). The return value of bufPrint is now discarded with `_ =`. No formatting or layout change: the rendered output is byte-identical to the pre-fix output modulo the crash.

dead_code_removed.claim: the `if (s1.len < 3)` padding branch next to the deleted @memcpy could never fire
dead_code_removed.evidence: std.fmt.bufPrint(buf[0..3], "{d:>3}", .{v}) succeeds only when the formatted output fits in 3 bytes; the `:>3` specifier right-aligns into exactly width 3, so a successful call returns exactly 3 bytes. Values needing more (|v| >= 100, e.g. +127 or -128 as i8) fail bufPrint and land in the catch, which writes '???' and continues. There is no path where s1.len < 3 on success. Branch removed with the @memcpy.
dead_code_removed.probe: zig run on {d:>3} for i8 5/12/0/-8/99/-99: all return exactly 3 bytes (' +5','+12',' +0',' -8','+99','-99'); i8 127 → '+127' (4 bytes, bufPrint fails).

rendering_note.discovery: Zig 0.16's {d} prints the sign for signed integer types: i8 12 formats as '+12', i8 0 as ' +0', i8 -8 as ' -8' (probed standalone: i8/i16/i32 signed → sign always; u8 and comptime_int literals → no '+'). legal_fixed values are i8, so every cell carries an explicit sign. The T327 test's golden text (+12, +0 forms) was correct all along; its explanatory comment ('{d:>3} shows the explicit sign on positive zero') was wrong about the mechanism and has been corrected.
rendering_note.impact: none on output — the fix preserves the exact rendering the (never-passing) golden described.
